newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdynia shipyard clears new share issue.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdynia shipyard clears new share issue.

text.p: The shareholders of the ailing Gdynia shipyard on Tuesday approved a new share issue of between 45 and 151 million zlotys, which could pave the way for the creation of a large shipbuilding group in Poland.

Gdynia's yard president Janusz Szlanta told Reuters that the issue, whose price and subscription date would be decided by the firm's supervisory board, would be primarily directed to the Stocznia Szczecinska shipyard. @

Under the government programme, the Szczecin company, Poland's most succesful shipyard is to be a leader of a shipbuilding industry group encompassing Gdynia, ship-engine maker H. Cegielski and possibly a steel mill and a bank.
"Our proposal will be primarily directed at Szczecin shipyard," Szlanta said. Gdynia's current share capital is 151 million zlotys.
Industrial sources have earlier said that Gdynia managers are divided over whether the company should join the holding or seek a separate investor. @

The firm's trade director Andrzej Buczkowski said the issue would be offered to all interested investors and not just to Szczecin shipyard. "The issue is an open one, it could be taken by any interested party," Buczkowski told Reuters.
The government has said that the creation of the shipbuilding holding was the only chance for the industry to weather foreign competition in the longer term.

Last month, the government, tired of waiting for results of talks among the group's would-be members, said it would kick-start the plan by letting Szczecin yard manage the treasury's 46 percent stake in Gdynia shipyard. @
Finance Minister Marek Belka said Poland's state-owned Bank Handlowy would also hand over its 18 percent stake in Gdynia to Szczecin.
Gdynia's other leading shareholder is state-owned Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA bank, which holds a 18.7 percent stake.
The Szczecin shipyard is now controlled 34.7 percent by its employees and 30 percent by a group of four Polish banks.
